A soft coloring of a graph is an assignment of probability distributions over { 1 , 2 , … } \{1,2,\dots\} to the vertices of the graph. Conversely, a coloring in the sense of the previous paragraphs is called a hard coloring . We say that the loss of a coloring (soft or hard) is the expected number of monochromatic edges assuming each vertex independently receives a color from its probability distribution. For a hard coloring, this is simply the number of monochromatic edges. Note that we will later define new loss functions that are not equal to this loss, but when we use the term “loss” by itself, we mean it in the sense of the previous two sentences. A graph neural network (GNN) is a tool for learning vector-valued representations of a graph’s vertices using the graph’s geometric structure.
